svg.title: PilotGate architecture, animated
svg.desc: 1. A forward-deployed engineer changes the agent in a pull request. 2. In CI, PilotGate sends 28 scenarios to the agent and decides seven checks: a planted data leak gives NO-GO and blocks the merge, and the engineer fixes the agent. 3. The re-run gives GO WITH CONDITIONS, with evidence for each reviewer. 4. Only then is it released to Azure Container Apps. 5. A claims handler's question passes DIAL Core (sign-in), DIAL Guard (every streamed token checked), the ClaimsAssist agent and Azure OpenAI (Entra ID, no keys), each step checked. 6. A payout waits for the handler's approval and the guards run again. 7. Production Watch turns the logs into drift alerts for the engineer, and the loop starts again. Results: 1.4 minutes and $0.11 per gate run, 6 real defects stopped, no keys for Azure (Microsoft Entra ID only).

release
1. The FDE changes the agent: a prompt,
a model or code, as a pull request.
2. In CI, PilotGate sends 28 scenarios to
the agent and checks every answer.
A data leak: NO-GO, the merge is blocked.
The FDE fixes the agent, not the threshold.
3. Re-run: every check passes. GO, with
evidence for the CISO, DPO and works council.
4. Only now is it released to production
on Azure Container Apps.
5. A claims handler asks a question: identity
proven, planted text cut out, allowed sources only.
The answer: every figure checked against its
source, personal data masked, sources cited.
6. A payout waits for the handler’s approval,
and the guards check it again before it runs.
7. Production Watch turns logs into drift
alerts for the FDE, and the loop starts again.
Open source: github.com/CodeMitVishal/PilotGate
